messages:
ryan: Hey - new prod alert. Customer hit 413 when sending gzipped embeddings batch with mixed dims (64 + 1536). They expected automatic splitting. Should router split for them or return 413 with hints? 

simon: Short answer: server-side split would be friendlier but has policy/quotas implications. We already charge per resulting chunk, right? :thinking:

anna: We currently return 413 for anything over bytes limit. Router doesn't attempt split because of complexity (dim compatibility + batching semantics).

keith: Also important: Dedicated tenants expect all requests to be accounted exactly. Auto-splitting server-side could hide original request shape and make debugging harder.

ryan: Ops report says most callers use vanilla client; schrodinger case is compressed payloads where Content-Length < limit but decompressed > limit. We detect after decompress -> 413.

simon: Could we add preflight endpoint or response header that predicts split plan? e.g., X-Embed-Estimate: units=420; splits=3

anna: I like preflight + console preview. Console could show "Preview split: 3 batches, est units: 420" before rollout.

keith: Telemetry question: tag whether split happened server-side vs client-side vs rejection. We need metrics for cost spikes and for quota enforcement.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling out feature flag ingress.autosplit-server -> off by default. :white_check_mark:

simon: Implementation sketch: do not mutate request body until we confirm tenant opt-in. Steps:
1) preflight header negotiation (client sends X-Embed-Preview:1)
2) router returns X-Embed-Estimate + split plan
3) client retries with Accept-Splits: server

code:
```
resp headers:
X-Embed-Estimate: units=442; splits=3; bytes=2097152
X-Embed-Plan: chunk_sizes=[512,512,1024]
```

anna: UX: console should surface per-tenant "estimated units" on the traffic dashboard, and show examples of how a given request would be split (toggle by sample payload).

keith: Quota enforcement: if tenant has monthly commit, server-side split is fine but we must surface per-chunk billing in usage API. For free-tier, fast-fail is better to avoid surprise charges.

ryan: Rollout plan suggestion: opt-in can be enabled per-tenant via console (checkbox), and we ship telemetry events: embed.split_plan_generated, embed.split_executed, embed.rejected_oversize.

simon: Related: router should prefer splitting across same model variant to keep latency predictable. If not possible, fallback to sequential splits (and mark has_multi_model=true in telemetry).

anna: Also add a console alert when split rate > 0.5% spikes. Engineering ops want an onboarding note for sales when enabling.

keith: Edge-case: mixed dims in the same batch may be incompatible for single model; server-side split must never coerce dims; only split along request boundaries.

ryan: Cool. Next steps: simon to prototype headers + sample API; anna to design console preview UI; keith to write telemetry schema + billing hooks. Opt-in feature flag created.

simon: I'll open RFC and proto PR later today. Thanks.
